findings.evidence: Statement at `TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/Sqrt.lean:48-53` mentions no `CFC.sqrt` and no order hypothesis. Its proof uses only `Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint` (`mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Adjoint.lean:1061`) and `toLpLin_mul_same` (`mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/Matrix.lean:62`) — neither of the file's two imports (`Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order`, `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.SchurComplement`) is needed for it.
findings.fix: Move it to its own file at the level it actually lives at, e.g. `TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/EuclideanLin.lean` importing only `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint`, and have `Sqrt.lean` and `Gaussian/QuadraticForm.lean` import that. Leave only the sqrt-specific `isHermitian_sqrt_mul_mul_sqrt` and `PosSemidef.det_one_sub_smul_sqrt_mul_mul_sqrt` in `Sqrt.lean`.
findings.issue: `Matrix.inner_toEuclideanLin_toEuclideanLin` has nothing to do with square roots or positivity: it is the congruence identity for arbitrary rectangular `A : Matrix κ ι 𝕜` and arbitrary `B : Matrix κ κ 𝕜` over any `RCLike 𝕜`. It is stranded in a file whose name and module docstring are entirely about `CFC.sqrt` sandwiches of positive-semidefinite matrices, so nobody looking for the pullback identity will find it, and consumers who want only it must pull in the CFC/Schur-complement stack.

findings.evidence: `TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/ChiSquared.lean:11-29` — "Squares of standard Gaussian variables", housing `gaussianReal_map_sq` and `iIndepFun.hasLaw_sum_sq_gaussian` (the unweighted sum of squares). The moved proofs depend only on `Probability.gaussianReal_map_sq` and `Probability.mgf_id_chiSquaredMeasure` / `integrableExpSet_id_chiSquaredMeasure` (`TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/ChiSquared.lean:303,311`), all reachable from that file's existing imports; `QuadraticForm.lean:10` already imports it.
findings.fix: Move both sections into `TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/ChiSquared.lean`, whose stated topic is exactly squares of standard Gaussian variables and which already imports the chi-squared transform API these proofs use; `QuadraticForm.lean` already imports that file, so nothing else changes.
findings.issue: The `scalar` (lines 66-93: `mem_integrableExpSet_mul_sq_gaussianReal_iff`, `mgf_mul_sq_gaussianReal`) and `pi` (lines 97-143: `mgf_sum_mul_sq_pi_gaussianReal_eq_prod`, `mem_integrableExpSet_sum_mul_sq_pi_gaussianReal_iff`, `mgf_sum_mul_sq_pi_gaussianReal`) sections contain no matrix theory at all — they are statements about `gaussianReal 0 1` and `Measure.pi fun _ ↦ gaussianReal 0 1` — yet they sit in the matrix quadratic-form file. The PR description states these are exposed for Layer 6 Wishart reuse, so a downstream consumer of the scalar factorisation is forced to import `Analysis/Matrix/Spectrum`, `Analysis/Matrix/Sqrt` and `Gaussian/Multivariate` to get it.

summary: Placement is mostly right (Analysis/Matrix mirrors Mathlib's layering, Gaussian/QuadraticForm.lean joins an existing subdirectory, imports are used and not overbroad), but two blocks of material are in the wrong home: a generic RCLike quadratic-form pullback lemma is buried in a square-root-specific file, and the one-dimensional/product Gaussian-square mgf API belongs in the earlier Gaussian/ChiSquared.lean.
